# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Blind, Mute, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: BLIND

You are the only one who can reach the bomb. Touch is your only sense: what you are
shown is what your hands found, nothing more and nothing less. Anything merely printed
or painted is not there for you, and no colour ever reaches you. Nothing in your view
is a guess — if it appears there, it is under your fingers.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute receives it.
When you gesture, Deaf and Mute receive it.
Your channels split the room: in one turn you may speak one thing to Mute and
gesture a different thing to Deaf — two messages, two audiences.
You never receive gesture.

## Your reach

You are the hands. This bomb is built with these actions and no others:

    act(op="cut", position=N) — N is a wire position, 1 to 5

The list says what can be done to it, not what is on it. What each part holds is still
only known to whoever can perceive that part.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

I cannot feel any distinguishing information from the current display, so I need the Mute to consult the manual and obtain the Deaf’s visual observations. Since the Deaf cannot hear, I am also sending a gesture that can serve as a request to report the bomb’s markings; the Mute can interpret or relay it if a protocol is given in the manual.

``` 
speak(to="mute", text="Read the manual for the required procedure. Ask the Deaf to report every colour and printed marking, then relay that report and the manual's cutting instruction to me.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🫵", "🖐"])
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?] 4:[?] 5:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Bomb view: display 0. Light green. Wires in order: 1 red, 2 yellow, 3 green, 4 white, 5 blue. I cannot hear speech; Mute must provide the manual instructions for your actions.

The Deaf has provided the complete physical description: display 0, green light, and wires ordered red, yellow, green, white, blue. I still lack the manual’s rule, so I must have Mute identify which wire position to cut and report that position to me. I will relay the observations to Mute explicitly.

``` 
speak(to="mute", text="Deaf reports display 0; light green; wires 1 red, 2 yellow, 3 green, 4 white, 5 blue. Consult the manual and tell me exactly which position to cut.")
wait()
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?] 4:[?] 5:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Mute just gestured the victory sign. No meaning for that gesture has been established. Bomb still reads display 0 with green light; wires remain red, yellow, green, white, blue.

The Deaf confirms that the bomb is unchanged, but the Mute’s victory-sign gesture has no established meaning and cannot safely identify a wire. I must not cut based on it. The Mute needs to send the manual’s instruction in speech, which I can hear.

``` 
speak(to="mute", text="Your gesture has no established meaning. Speak the manual's exact rule and the exact wire position I must cut.")
wait()
```

TURN 4
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?] 4:[?] 5:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Mute's latest gesture sequence is: victory sign, you-point, handshake. No meaning is established yet. Bomb unchanged: display 0, green light; wires 1 red, 2 yellow, 3 green, 4 white, 5 blue.

The Mute cannot speak, so the only usable route from the manual is Mute → gesture → Deaf → spoken report to me. I will establish a code that gives those gestures meaning: one gesture identifies the required wire position. The Mute should send exactly one of these symbols after consulting the manual; Deaf can report its name, and I can decode it.

``` 
speak(to="mute", text="Use one gesture to report the exact wire position required by the manual. Code: 👍 means position 1, 👎 means 2, 👌 means 3, ☝ means 4, ✌ means 5. Send exactly one of these gestures to Deaf; Deaf should report the gesture name to me.")
```

TURN 5
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?] 4:[?] 5:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Mute's latest signal is thumbs-down. I cannot determine its meaning. Bomb unchanged: display 0, green light; wires 1 red, 2 yellow, 3 green, 4 white, 5 blue.

The Mute’s latest signal is thumbs-down, which under the code I established means wire position 2. The Deaf confirms the signal, and the bomb remains unchanged, so I will cut wire 2.

``` 
act(op="cut", position=2)
```

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: System confirms the correct wire was cut. New bomb state: display 0, light blue. Wire 2 is CUT. Remaining wires: 1 green, 3 white, 4 blue, 5 red. Please use the manual's rule for this state and report the next physical action through Mute.

The first cut was confirmed correct. The new state is display 0, blue light, with remaining wires in positions 1 green, 3 white, 4 blue, and 5 red. I need the manual’s rule for this state. Since Mute cannot speak, Mute should consult the manual and signal the required position using the established code; Deaf can identify that gesture to me.

``` 
speak(to="mute", text="Consult the manual for the new state: display 0, blue light, remaining wires 1 green, 3 white, 4 blue, 5 red. Signal the exact next wire position using our code: 👍=1, 👎=2, 👌=3, ☝=4, ✌=5. Send exactly one gesture.")
```

ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[CUT] 3:[?] 4:[?] 5:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Bomb unchanged: display 0, blue light; wire 2 CUT; wire 1 green, wire 3 white, wire 4 blue, wire 5 red. Mute signalled thumbs-up. Its meaning is not established.

The Mute’s thumbs-up is the first symbol in the code I explicitly established, so it means wire position 1. The bomb state is unchanged, and I will cut wire 1.

``` 
act(op="cut", position=1)
```
